questions.prompt: Which collection keeps insertion order and allows duplicates?
questions.explanation: A List such as ArrayList is ordered and allows duplicates. Sets reject duplicates (HashSet has no guaranteed order; TreeSet sorts).

questions.prompt: `driver.findElements(...)` returns an empty list when nothing matches, while `findElement(...)` throws NoSuchElementException.
questions.explanation: That difference is why findElements(...).isEmpty() is the usual way to assert that something is absent.

questions.prompt: Which Map would you use to count how many products appear in each category?
questions.explanation: Category name (String) maps to a count (Integer). A List or Set cannot associate a count with each key.
A Set ignores the duplicate "a", leaving three elements.

questions.prompt: This loop throws ConcurrentModificationException. Why, and what is the fix?
options: Removing from a list while iterating it with for-each invalidates the iterator; use removeIf(s -> s.isBlank()) or an Iterator's remove()
isBlank is not a String method
The list must be a LinkedList
questions.explanation: The enhanced for loop uses an iterator that detects structural changes made outside it. removeIf or iterator.remove() modify the list safely. (isBlank exists since Java 11.)

questions.prompt: Which is an unchecked exception (you are not forced to catch or declare it)?
questions.explanation: Selenium's exceptions extend WebDriverException, a RuntimeException, so they are unchecked. IOException, FileNotFoundException and InterruptedException are checked.
The exception from parseInt is caught (printing 'catch'), and finally always runs.

questions.prompt: A helper `isDisplayed(By by)` catches every Exception and returns false. Tests using it pass even when the locator has a typo in the CSS syntax. What is the better design?
options: Catch only NoSuchElementException (the expected 'not present' case) and let other exceptions such as InvalidSelectorException fail the test
Remove the try/catch and let NoSuchElementException fail every absence check
Log the exception and return true
questions.explanation: Catch only what you expect and can handle. A broad catch converts real errors (bad selectors, dead sessions) into false negatives. Catching nothing makes the helper useless for absence checks.

questions.prompt: You need to verify that a table's 'Invoice' column is sorted descending by date and has no duplicate invoice numbers. Which combination fits best?
options: Collect invoice numbers into a List and compare its size with a HashSet of the same values; collect dates as LocalDate into a List and compare it with a copy sorted in reverse order
Use an array and print it
questions.explanation: Size differences between a List and a Set reveal duplicates, and comparing to a sorted copy checks order. Parsing to LocalDate avoids lexicographic mistakes with date strings.

coding.title: Find duplicate values
coding.prompt:
Write a class `TableChecks` with a static method `java.util.List<String> duplicates(java.util.List<String> values)` returning each value that appears more than once, **in the order of its second occurrence**, listed once.

Example: `duplicates(List.of("INV-1", "INV-2", "INV-1", "INV-3", "INV-2", "INV-1"))` returns `[INV-1, INV-2]`.
coding.explanation: Set.add returns false when the value is already present, which detects the second occurrence in one pass. A LinkedHashSet keeps insertion order and ignores the third occurrence, so each duplicate is reported once in the order it was found.
hints: Set.add() returns false if the element was already there.
Use one set for values seen and another for duplicates.
coding.runInstructions: Create a Maven project with JUnit 5 (`org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter`, scope `test`). Put `TableChecks.java` in `src/main/java/` and `TableChecksTest.java` in `src/test/java/`. Run `mvn test`; all tests should pass.

coding.title: Count by status and fail clearly
coding.prompt: Write a class `StatusCounter` with a static method `java.util.Map<String, Integer> count(java.util.List<String> statuses)` that counts each status, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, and stores keys in upper case (e.g. `" paid"` and `"PAID"` both count as `PAID`). Keys must be in alphabetical order (use a TreeMap). If any status is null or blank, throw `IllegalArgumentException` with a message containing the **row index** (0-based), e.g. `"blank status at row 2"`.
coding.explanation: Map.merge adds 1 to an existing count or inserts 1 for a new key, which keeps counting to one line. A TreeMap sorts keys so assertions and reports are deterministic. Throwing an unchecked exception with the row index makes bad data easy to locate, which is better than silently skipping it.
hints: Use an index loop so you can put i in the exception message.
coding.runInstructions: Create a Maven project with JUnit 5 (`org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter`, scope `test`). Put `StatusCounter.java` in `src/main/java/` and `StatusCounterTest.java` in `src/test/java/`. Run `mvn test`; all tests should pass.
